pharm: Directly stimulates uterine smooth muscle (and partial alpha-adrenergic/serotonergic activity) to produce sustained tetanic uterine contractions.
quick: Oral 0.2 mg 3-4 times daily in the puerperium, up to 1 week
May be taken without regard to food
Small amounts in milk; short courses generally acceptable
Avoid; no benefit and may worsen effects
Blood pressure, uterine tone, signs of vasospasm
summary: Methylergometrine (methylergonovine) is an ergot-alkaloid uterotonic used after delivery to manage uterine atony, hemorrhage, and subinvolution and to control postpartum bleeding. It produces strong, sustained uterine contractions and is a vasoconstrictor, so it is contraindicated in hypertension, toxemia, and pregnancy. Excess or sensitive response can cause severe hypertension and vasospasm.
indications: Routine management after delivery of the placenta for uterine atony, hemorrhage, and subinvolution of the uterus
Control of uterine hemorrhage in the second stage of labor following delivery of the anterior shoulder

dosage.d: 0.2 mg (one tablet) 3 or 4 times daily in the puerperium

dosage.c: Acute postpartum hemorrhage (parenteral, per other labeling)
dosage.d: 0.2 mg IM; may repeat every 2-4 hours as needed
dosage.n: IV route only for emergencies, given slowly with BP monitoring

admin: For routine puerperal use, give orally 0.2 mg three to four times daily for up to one week
Reserve intravenous administration for life-threatening emergencies; inject slowly over at least 60 seconds with blood pressure monitoring
Monitor blood pressure, especially with parenteral use
Do not use to induce labor or before delivery of the placenta in routine practice
Avoid concomitant potent vasoconstrictors and strong CYP3A4 inhibitors
moa: Methylergometrine acts directly on uterine smooth muscle to increase the tone, rate, and amplitude of rhythmic contractions, producing a sustained tetanic contraction that mechanically compresses uterine blood vessels and reduces postpartum bleeding. As an ergot alkaloid it also has partial agonist/antagonist activity at alpha-adrenergic and serotonergic receptors, accounting for its vasoconstrictor effects.

relative: Obliterative vascular disease / coronary artery disease
Concomitant strong CYP3A4 inhibitors or other vasoconstrictors
monitor: Signs of peripheral or coronary vasospasm

preg: Contraindicated during pregnancy; it is a potent uterotonic intended only for use after delivery. Inadvertent use during pregnancy can cause sustained uterine contraction and fetal harm.
lact: Small amounts are excreted in breast milk; short postpartum courses are generally considered acceptable. Avoid prolonged use, and observe the infant; ergot alkaloids may theoretically reduce milk production.
renal: Use with caution in renal impairment; reduced clearance may increase the risk of toxicity.
hepatic: Methylergometrine is hepatically metabolized (CYP3A4); use with caution in hepatic impairment and avoid strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, which can precipitate ergotism.

major: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (azole antifungals, macrolides, HIV protease inhibitors) - risk of severe ergotism (vasospasm, ischemia)
Triptans and other ergot alkaloids - additive vasospasm
moderate: Bromocriptine and other dopamine agonists (additive vascular effects)
interactions.food: May be taken without regard to food.
interactions.diagnostics: May elevate blood pressure readings; no specific assay interference of note.

rare: Acute myocardial infarction (rare, reported especially after IV use)
emergency: Hypertensive crisis with seizure or stroke

monitoring: Uterine tone and amount of bleeding
Signs of vasospasm (chest pain, cold/painful extremities, headache)
counsel: This medicine helps your womb contract and reduces bleeding after delivery
Report severe headache, chest pain, numbness or cold/painful fingers or toes, or visual changes immediately
Tell your doctor if you have high blood pressure
Cramping abdominal pain is expected as the womb contracts
Do not take other ergot or migraine medicines while on this drug
pk: Oral 5-15 minutes; IM 2-5 minutes; IV immediate
Store tablets at 20-25 C; protect from light; injection refrigerate and protect from light
pearls: Potent uterotonic and vasoconstrictor - contraindicated in hypertension, preeclampsia/eclampsia, and pregnancy
Reserve IV use for emergencies and give slowly with blood pressure monitoring (risk of hypertensive crisis)
Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors can precipitate ergotism - avoid combining
Second-line to oxytocin for postpartum hemorrhage; useful when oxytocin is insufficient
Limit oral courses to about one week
missed: Take a missed dose as soon as you remember; if it is almost time for the next dose, skip it and resume the schedule. Do not double up. Courses are short (up to one week).
overdose: Overdose (ergotism) causes hypertension, nausea/vomiting, numbness/tingling, cold extremities, vasospasm with gangrene, seizures, and cardiovascular collapse. Treat supportively; control hypertension and vasospasm with vasodilators (e.g., nitroprusside, nitroglycerin) and provide anticonvulsants and circulatory support as needed.
